panels.description: Serving state per engine. PAUSED (grey) means the idle-drain policy withheld a healthy engine from routing to save idle power - it is not a fault. Health is multiplied by the drain state so a stopped engine still reads DOWN, never PAUSED; the trailing `or (ramjet_upstream_up * 0)` keeps the panel working when idle-drain is off and exports no drain series.
panels.title: Engine readiness

panels.description: Current free space on the node's /prod model volume. Storage changes slowly, so a point-in-time capacity stat is more useful here than a full-width time series.
panels.title: Model storage free

panels.description: Current average kernel activity across all eight GPUs. This is nvidia-smi kernel activity, not Model FLOP/s Utilization.
panels.title: GPU compute avg

panels.description: Current average GPU memory-controller activity. This measures reads and writes, not VRAM allocation.
panels.title: Memory activity avg

panels.description: Current average framebuffer allocation across the eight 96 GB GPUs. This includes model weights and KV cache.
panels.title: VRAM allocated avg

panels.description: Current maximum core temperature across the node. The cards begin throttling around 83–85°C.
panels.title: Hottest GPU

panels.description: Current one-minute average board power summed across all eight GPUs; the combined enforced limit is 4.8 kW.
panels.title: GPU power total

panels.description: Lowest current streaming-multiprocessor clock as a percentage of that GPU's reported maximum. Compare with load and throttling before treating a low idle value as a problem.
panels.title: Lowest SM clock
Time per output token p50 / p95

panels.description: Fraction of each sampling window in which an NVIDIA kernel was running. High is usually desirable for this inference workload, but this is not Model FLOP/s Utilization (MFU); correlate it with token throughput, memory activity, power and clocks.
panels.title: GPU kernel activity

panels.description: Fraction of time GPU memory was being read or written. This is memory-controller activity, not the amount of VRAM allocated; sustained high memory activity with lower kernel activity can indicate a memory-bound decode workload.
panels.title: GPU memory activity

panels.description: Per-GPU core temperature. These cards begin thermal throttling around 83–85°C; alerting intentionally waits for a sustained 90°C condition.
panels.title: GPU temperature

panels.description: One-minute average board power per GPU. Power and temperature help distinguish productive compute from a misleadingly high kernel-activity signal; each card has a 600 W enforced limit.
panels.title: GPU power draw

panels.description: Streaming-multiprocessor clock as a percentage of the reported maximum. Falling clocks during sustained work point toward power or thermal throttling.
panels.title: GPU SM clock vs max

panels.description: Number of active power/thermal slowdown reasons per GPU. Any non-zero state means clocks are being limited by a software power cap, thermal condition, or hardware power brake.
panels.title: GPU throttling

panels.description: Per-upstream drain state. warm = routable; draining = fenced from new routing while in-flight work finishes; drained = fenced and quiet, so the separately privileged actor may stop the container. In observe mode the state machine advances and publishes intent but fences nothing.
panels.title: Idle drain state

panels.description: The two inputs the privileged actor converges on: it stops an engine only when desired running is no AND safe to stop is yes, and starts it as soon as desired running is yes. Neither value is a fault. safe to stop means the upstream is fenced and quiet, so stopping it cannot interrupt a request the load balancer already dispatched.
panels.title: Stop intent (desired running / safe to stop)

panels.description: Whether the fleet as a whole is inside its configured idle window. This is the precondition for draining anything, so it explains why a replica did or did not park. Presence of this series also means the policy is enabled at all: nothing in this row is exported while the mode is off.
panels.title: Fleet idle window

panels.description: Drain state transitions per hour, by upstream and target state. This is the flapping detector: qualifying observe mode requires a clean interval here before enforcement, because a badly tuned idle threshold shows up as repeated draining/warm churn rather than as an error. Restoring the warm floor runs on every tick, so a park that was safe when made can be reversed without any request arriving.
panels.title: Drain transitions (per hour)
